newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil trades at new five-year high.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil trades at new five-year high.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil traded on Friday at a new five-year high of $30.60 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, traders said.
The sale between a European major to a Singapore trader for a 150,000-barrel cargo loading on November 26-30 was five cents more than the previous record chalked up in mid-October.
The same trader is currently negotiating with another European major to buy a second 150,000-barrel cargo for loading in early December at $30.60 fob Singapore.
Gas oil prices in Singapore held their own over the past few weeks despite falling prices in the west due to strong regional demand for prompt barrels.
Indonesia more than doubled its regular monthly imports in November to between five and six million barrels and China is still seen seeking barrels for late November arrival.
One cargo was sold earlier this week at $235 per tonne cost-and-freight South China for late November arrival.
Higher Singapore prices also opened the arbitrage for exports from North West Europe and the Mediterrenean to India, traders said.
